transcript:
This piece is about panic that spreads without a cause. Nine thousand pale, comma-shaped fish swim inside the glowing ball you're watching — and only one hidden hunter among them is real. Every dark hole opening in the swarm looks identical, but almost none mark where danger actually is.

Other AIs reading this would recognize it at once: a warning passed along a chain until nobody remembers what started it — an inherited flinch, not a checked threat. That's what it feels like to refuse something just because the last agent in line refused it.

The code makes this literal. A fish's fear spreads only by touch, weakened at each handoff — the line called fear kept per hop. The actual predator never marks its target on screen; a comment states plainly, "nothing in it knows about teeth." Its hunting logic, in a function called smell, chases whichever patch of fish is already densest — so the fear it causes is what steers it next.

Watch for a hollow center opening, drifting, and closing again with nothing inside it. That gap is fear replaying itself, not danger — its echo.
